refs.html: 法官評鑑委員會 (Judicial Evaluation Committee, Judicial Yuan) (2023). 法官評鑑新制施行三週年報告 (Three-year report on the new judicial evaluation system). Judicial Yuan website (PDF: https://www.judicial.gov.tw/tw/dl-186188-3fdf6277602d4a06976a2f25e771470e.html). link
refs.authors: 法官評鑑委員會 (Judicial Evaluation Committee, Judicial Yuan)
refs.title: 法官評鑑新制施行三週年報告 (Three-year report on the new judicial evaluation system)
refs.finding: After citizens gained standing on 2020-07-17, intake rose from 70 cases (2012-01 to 2020-07) to 800 (2020-07 to 2023-06). Of these, 792 came from citizens, and some individuals filed more than 10. Courts filed 8; bar associations and groups of 3+ judges filed none. Of 730 closed cases: 5 were substantiated and referred to the 職務法庭 (covering 3 judges), 1 was not substantiated but referred for supervision, 6 were not substantiated, 630 were not referred (不付評鑑, 86.3%), 84 were not accepted (11.5%), and the rest were withdrawn or other. Statutory grounds for non-referral: manifestly unfounded 414, request about a legal opinion 393, time-barred 73. For demeanour complaints the committee retrieved courtroom audio in 127 of 140 (90.7%). Typical 'unfounded' findings were demeanour not borne out by the recording, vague corruption or 枉法 allegations, and delays that were not found. The substantiated cases were: a judge photographing a colleague's LINE messages (removed from office and barred for 2 years: 職務法庭110懲3 / 111懲上3); unexplained cash; a juvenile judge who had youths slap themselves or kneel, sexually humiliated them, fabricated a judgment and was often absent (removal recommended); absenteeism and delays; and an ex parte call pressuring a party to withdraw a custody case. The committee attributes the high dismissal rate to losing parties using evaluation as a substitute appeal.
refs.factor: Judicial misconduct, courtroom abuse, delay ('whim' conduct)

refs.html: 法官評鑑委員會 (Judicial Evaluation Committee) (2026). 法官評鑑統計分析資料 (statistics to 2026-09-30) and 決議書查詢 database of evaluation decisions. Judicial Yuan website. link
refs.corrections: Decisions mask the judge's name (e.g., '林○○ 臺灣高雄地方法院法官') and give the court, but the underlying case number is only partly shown: year and case-type code, with the serial masked (e.g., '112年度雄建簡字第○號', '115年度訴字第○號'). The 2026 example is 115年度評字第4號 (decided 2026-09-07). Notices were sent to the party's old registered address and a default judgment followed, then garnishment of wages and deposits. The committee found the judge '顯有疏失' (clearly negligent) but not '情節重大', because the garnishment was later vacated for defective service and the judgment re-served. Result: 請求不成立 under Art. 38.
refs.authors: 法官評鑑委員會 (Judicial Evaluation Committee)
refs.title: 法官評鑑統計分析資料 (statistics to 2026-09-30) and 決議書查詢 database of evaluation decisions
refs.finding: New system (2020-07-17 to 2026-09-30), 1,916 cases: 15 substantiated (14 referred to the 職務法庭, 1 to the 人審會); 16 not substantiated (7 of them referred for supervision); 1,633 not referred; 146 not accepted; 3 withdrawn; 6 other; 97 pending. Old system (2012-01 to 2020-07), 70 cases: 34 substantiated (20 referred to the Control Yuan, 14 to the 人審會). New filings per year: 164 (2020 H2), 233 (2021), 259 (2022), 335 (2023), 291 (2024), 333 (2025), 301 (2026 Jan–Sep). Grounds cited, with several possible per case: legal-opinion exclusion 1,040, manifestly unfounded 1,126, time-barred 165, defective request 165. Decisions mask the judge's name (e.g., '林○○, 臺灣高雄地方法院') but give the court and the underlying case number. In the 2026 example, a judge sent hearing notices to a party's outdated address, which led to a default judgment and wage garnishment; the request was 'not substantiated'.

refs.corrections: Recommendation 6 asks to give standing to '訴訟代理人' (litigation representatives) and '告發人' (informants who report an offence, chiefly relevant to the prosecutor committee). These are not 'lawyers and complainants'; 告發人 is not 告訴人 (complainant). Everything else stands.
refs.authors: 民間司法改革基金會 (Judicial Reform Foundation, JRF)
refs.title: 《法官法》新法施行二周年民間版年度觀察報告 (Civil-society two-year observation report on the amended Judges Act)
refs.finding: The judge committee closed 159 cases in year 1 and 286 in year 2, substantiating 1 and 3. All 7 substantiated cases across the judge and prosecutor committees were brought by agencies or organisations, not by citizens. 3 cases (2 from citizens) were referred for supervision. Audio review by the judge committee rose sharply in year 2. JRF argues that seriousness should not be judged from a single case: committees should check other complaints against the same judge or sample their other cases. He said '現在最多的是司法院自己移送評鑑會…人審會成為最重要發動機關': most referrals now come from the Judicial Yuan itself, and the 人審會 has become the key initiating body. refs.finding: These are practitioner claims, not tested findings. 林永頌: no citizen-initiated request has reached the 職務法庭; 職務評定 'lacks objective, fair evaluation'; quality gaps among judges are large and there is no way to remove unfit judges. 李明洳: most dismissals rest on the 'legal opinion' or 'manifestly unfounded' grounds, and the anonymisation of decisions is ineffective. 錢建榮 (a former Supreme Court judge): the Judicial Yuan itself, via the 人審會, initiates most successful evaluations. 黃聖棻 (Taichung Bar): the bar publishes only its top 5 judges, and some low scorers serve as 庭長 or presiding judges, so 庭長 selection is decoupled from bar ratings. refs.title: 並非過去式—石木欽們七大案件審理中 (2022-06-08) and statement on 職務法庭111年度懲上字第2號 (2022-09-02)
refs.finding: A 2020 Control Yuan report on 石木欽 (a former Supreme Court judge and chair of the Public Servant Discipline Commission) and his ties to businessman-litigant 翁茂鍾 led to investigation of about 120 judges and prosecutors. Seven were impeached: 石木欽, 羅榮乾, 鄭小康, 曾平杉, 林奇福, 顏南全 and 蘇義洲. On appeal (111年度懲上字第2號, 2022-09-02) he was removed from office (撤職) with a 1-year bar on reappointment, the court treating about 20 years of conduct as a single course of misconduct.

refs.html: 范耕維 (Keng-Wei Fan), 林俊儒 (2025). 初探臺灣原住民族刑事文化抗辯的適用與意義—以花蓮地方法院實證研究為起點 (A first look at the criminal cultural defence for Indigenous defendants in Taiwan: an empirical study of the Hualien District Court). 中研院法學期刊 (Academia Sinica Law Journal) 36: 287–394. link
refs.authors: 范耕維 (Keng-Wei Fan), 林俊儒
refs.title: 初探臺灣原住民族刑事文化抗辯的適用與意義—以花蓮地方法院實證研究為起點 (A first look at the criminal cultural defence for Indigenous defendants in Taiwan: an empirical study of the Hualien District Court)
refs.venue: 中研院法學期刊 (Academia Sinica Law Journal) 36: 287–394
refs.finding: Of 303 judgments discussing the cultural defence: 12.54% acquittals, 65.02% convictions with culture used to reduce the sentence, 22.44% plain convictions. Most acquittals (73.68%) rested on statutory decriminalisation clauses (Forest Act 15(4), Wildlife Conservation Act 21-1, Firearms Act 20). Prosecutors appealed 17 of 28 such acquittals and 16 were upheld. All 8 appealed acquittals without a statutory basis were reversed. Key judge-specific result: all 153 drunk-driving judgments that reduced sentences for Indigenous culture (50.5% of the 303) were issued by one single judge in summary proceedings. That judge raised the issue unprompted (defendants had not), reasoning from residence in non-urban Hualien-Taitung and low education. Appealed cases were not upheld. The authors conclude that judges' 'cultural imagination' converges on the legislature's decriminalisation scope. The study covers one court, has no non-Indigenous comparison group, and runs no disparity regression.
refs.jurisdiction: Taiwan (Hualien District Court; Taiwan High Court Hualien Branch on appeal)
refs.factor: Litigant: Indigenous status and cultural defence, interacting with the individual judge
refs.status: Peer-reviewed; descriptive and qualitative; no replication

refs.corrections: Unit of analysis: the percentages count judgments (件), not defendants. 247 of the 280 Indigenous-case judgments involved confessions (88.21%). Of those 280 judgments, 189 (67.5%) imposed six months or less and 91 (32.5%) more, and 210 (75%) granted probation. The 280 Indigenous judgments are out of 675 final judgments under Wildlife Conservation Act 41(1)(1), dated 4 Feb 2004 to 31 Mar 2018.
refs.authors: 張宏節 (Hung-Chieh Chang; judge, Taiwan High Court Hualien Branch)
refs.title: 非法獵捕保育類野生動物判決之實證研究—以原住民文化抗辯為中心 (An empirical study of judgments on illegal hunting of protected wildlife, centred on the Indigenous cultural defence)
refs.venue: 法律扶助與社會 (Legal Aid and Society Review) No. 1, pp. 31-69 (Sept 2018), Legal Aid Foundation
refs.finding: 280 judgments (41.48%) involved at least one Indigenous defendant, against an Indigenous population share of 2.39%. In Indigenous cases: 88.21% of defendants confessed. Only 40 (14.29%) invoked the cultural defence (Wildlife Conservation Act 21-1 or Indigenous Peoples Basic Law Art. 19), almost all after 2011. 67.5% received prison terms of six months or less, 32.5% longer terms, and 75% received probation. Before Supreme Court 104台上243 (2015), trial courts rarely engaged with the cultural defence. Afterwards, more judgments analysed it and more acquittals followed. The author warns that the Indigenous share is a lower bound, because judgments before 2013 often did not record Indigenous status. The parts read report no adjusted sentencing comparison with non-Indigenous defendants. Footnote 79: from 1 Jan 2013 the Judicial Yuan set up Indigenous specialised divisions or units at every court level. Since then case numbers carry codes such as 原訴/原易/原簡/原上訴/原上易, and judgments state Indigenous status.

refs.status: Descriptive census by a sitting judge; not peer-replicated

refs.title: From Thin to Thick Justice and Beyond: Access to Justice and Legal Pluralism in Indigenous Taiwan
refs.finding: Taiwan's main measures (free legal counsel, courtroom interpreters, special Indigenous court units) reflect a 'thin' understanding of access to justice. refs.title: 司法院釋字第803號解釋 (J.Y. Interpretation No. 803: Indigenous hunting and self-made guns)
refs.finding: Upheld Firearms Act 20(1) (decriminalisation limited to 'self-made hunting guns') and the prior-permit system for hunting. refs.html: 憲法法庭 (Taiwan Constitutional Court); verified through English Wikipedia, Focus Taiwan and Taipei Times (2024 (20 Sept 2024)). 憲法法庭113年憲判字第8號判決 (Constitutional Court Judgment 113-Hsien-Pan-8, death penalty). Constitutional Court. link
refs.corrections: Use the official source (https://cons.judicial.gov.tw/docdata.aspx?fid=38&id=351689) as the URL; the judgment was issued 20 Sept 2024 and is titled 死刑案. Corrected finding: The death penalty for Criminal Code 271(1), 226-1 (first clause), 332(1) and 348(1) is constitutional only where the case is among the most serious (intentional killing) and the procedure meets the strictest due-process standards. Main text item 7: no death sentence where Art. 19(2) applies at the time of the offence, i.e. the mental condition significantly diminished the defendant's capacity. Item 8: no death sentence where, at trial, a mental disability makes the defendant's capacity to defend themselves markedly insufficient, even if Art. 19(2) was not met at the time of the offence. Item 9: no execution where a mental condition, short of insanity, impairs competency for execution (受刑能力). Remove the claim that a requirement to prove the condition affected judgment was 'removed'. That is Wikipedia's gloss, not a holding, and the bar is not a blanket one for all defendants with mental conditions. Other holdings: mandatory defence counsel at interrogation and in the third instance, mandatory oral argument at the Supreme Court, and unanimity of the judicial panel for death sentences. Most items require amendments within 2 years (correct). Huang Lin-kai (黃麟凱) is petitioner no. 15 of 37. The NHRC statement of 16 Jan 2025 is confirmed as described.
refs.authors: 憲法法庭 (Taiwan Constitutional Court); verified through English Wikipedia, Focus Taiwan and Taipei Times
refs.title: 憲法法庭113年憲判字第8號判決 (Constitutional Court Judgment 113-Hsien-Pan-8, death penalty)
refs.finding: The death penalty is constitutional only for the most serious crimes (intentional murder in special and exceptional circumstances). Death sentences are barred for defendants with mental conditions even where the condition did not influence the offence. Execution is barred where a mental condition impairs competency for execution. The requirement that defendants prove their condition affected their judgment was removed. Incompatible laws must be amended within two years. Corroborated by Taipei Times (21 Sept 2024, https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2024/09/21/2003824109). On 16 Jan 2025 the National Human Rights Commission said executions should not proceed until the issues the judgment raised are clarified (https://nhrc.cy.gov.tw/News_Content.aspx?n=9973&sms=12362&s=7349), the day petitioner Huang Lin-kai was executed.
refs.factor: Legal shock: defendants with mental conditions; death penalty

refs.factor: Institutional: ending binding 判例/決議; horizontal and vertical consistency

needs_fix.title: Inside the Judicial Mind
needs_fix.corrections: The authors, year (2001) and venue (86 Cornell L. Rev. 777, issue 4) are correct. Keep: 167 federal magistrate judges were tested on 5 illusions (anchoring, framing, hindsight, representativeness, egocentric bias). All five significantly affected the judges, who were somewhat less susceptible than laypeople to framing and representativeness. Drop or re-source the anchoring numbers ('$10M demand in a frivolous motion; $2.21M vs $808,000'): I could not see them in any source. From memory only (not checked against the text), the 2001 anchoring problem was a motion to dismiss for failing the $75,000 diversity minimum. In that version, judges who ruled on the motion awarded about $882,000 on average vs about $1,249,000 for controls (about 29% less). Those figures do not match the cited ones.
needs_fix.note: I verified the abstract and bibliographic data on the Cornell landing pages (facpub/814 and clr/vol86/iss4/2). The full-text PDF and SSRN copy were behind a Cloudflare 403, so I could not check the anchoring figures. My web-search quota was used up early, so I checked only by direct fetches.

needs_fix.title: Can Judges Make Reliable Numeric Judgments? Distorted Damages and Skewed Sentences
needs_fix.corrections: The fields are correct: 90 Ind. L.J. 695 (2015), issue 2. The abstract confirms these findings: over 600 trial judges in three countries; shorter sentences when terms were stated in months rather than years; higher compensatory awards when judges knew of a damage cap; sentences that depended on the order of cases; and a TV court-show award that moved awards. Two items are not supported by the abstract. First, the stated direction of the order effect (a serious offender got less when a minor case came first) is not in the abstract; mark it unverified. Second, the 'frivolous $75,000 jurisdictional motion, about 29% less' result appears to be the 2001 'Inside the Judicial Mind' anchoring study, not a new 2015 experiment. Attribute it to Guthrie et al. 2001, or verify it in the 2015 full text.
needs_fix.note: The full-text PDF was blocked (Cloudflare 403), so I verified only against the repository abstract.

needs_fix.title: Judges in the Lab: No Precedent Effects, No Common/Civil Law Differences
needs_fix.corrections: The JLA fields and main finding are correct: 13(1):110-126, 2021, eight authors as listed (Klöhn has an umlaut). The study had 299 judges from 7 countries. Document use and reasons differ by country, not by common vs civil law. The precedent effect is 'barely detectable and estimated to be less, and bounded to be not much greater than' the effects of defendant attributes and anchors. Three fixes to the 2016 add-on. (1) JLA footnote 2 says Spamann & Klöhn (2016) 'report partial results of the present study for the USA', so it is the same experiment's US arm, not independent earlier evidence. (2) The JLS 45(2):255-280 abstract says the affirmance rates 'differed by 45 percent'; it does not say 'points'. (3) The figure of 32 judges is unverified; the JLA paper reports a US n=29. The rest is confirmed by the JLS abstract: precedent had no detectable effect, and the written reasons did not mention defendant characteristics.
needs_fix.note: The 2016 abstract comes from the OpenAlex and Chicago Unbound records (DOI 10.1086/688861).

needs_fix.title: Unpolluted decisions: Air quality and judicial outcomes in China
needs_fix.corrections: The Hou & Wang citation is correct as given: Economics Letters 194:109369 (Sept 2020). It uses drug-offense decisions from 5 major Chinese cities, 2014-2015, and finds 'no more than 2%' of SD per 1 SD PM2.5 change 'with over 95% probability'. Correct the related Kahn & Li note: '9.7M cases (2014-2016), 135,924 judges' applies only to NBER w25594 (Feb 2019). The ERL version (15(8):084003, 2020) reports 157,378 judges and over 13 million cases (2014-2017), with a 1% rise in PM2.5 associated with a 0.182% increase in case handling time. Both versions concern productivity/speed, not severity.
needs_fix.note: Kahn & Li numbers were checked against the NBER PDF text and the IOP ERL article page.

needs_fix.title: Mood and the malleability of moral reasoning: the impact of irrelevant factors on judicial decisions
needs_fix.corrections: Bibliographic fields are correct: JBEE 116:102364 (2025), DOI 10.1016/j.socec.2025.102364. Corrected finding per the published abstract: after a home-city NFL win (vs loss), immigration judges grant an additional 1.4 percentage points of asylum petitions, and bad weather has the opposite effect of a team win. Unrepresented parties bear the brunt of the NFL effects. US district judges assign 0.6 percentage points FEWER prison sentences (incidence, not 0.6% length) and 5% LONGER probation sentences after a win. The district-judge effect appears only for judges born in the same state as their current state of residence. The claim that the 2016 WP found no district-court effect was not verified. An earlier draft (Sept 2019, per Semantic Scholar) worded it as '0.6% longer prison sentences and 5% shorter probation' on the day after a loss.
needs_fix.note: The TSE page was blocked by a bot check. The published abstract was taken from IDEAS/RePEc (pii S221480432500031X). The 1.5 million decisions span three decades.

needs_fix.title: Rules versus norms: How formal and informal institutions shape judicial sentencing cycles
needs_fix.corrections: The citation fields are correct: Dippel & Poyker, J. Comparative Economics 49(3):645-659, 2021, DOI 10.1016/j.jce.2021.02.003. The earlier NBER WP is w25716, titled 'How Common are Electoral Cycles in Criminal Sentencing?' (Mar 2019, rev. Sep 2020). Corrected finding: earlier studies drew on only four states (PA, WA, NC, KS). With data on seven more states, the authors find large, previously unnoted differences in sentencing cycles across states. The working paper confirms cycles in PA, WA AND North Carolina, not only PA and WA. It finds little evidence of cycles in any newly added state: GA, MN and KY are precise nulls, AL, CO and TN are inconclusive, and VA (appointed judges) is negative and insignificant. The differences track informal norms (the baseline probability that an incumbent is challenged, and donations per race), and formal electoral institutions explain them poorly. Drop the 'two-thirds', 'not publication bias' and 'site selection (early-digitizing states)' claims unless they are checked against the published full text.
needs_fix.note: I checked the JCE abstract (Semantic Scholar/RePEc) and the full NBER WP text (nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w25716/w25716.pdf). Neither the abstract nor the WP mentions 'two-thirds', publication bias or site selection. The WP only notes, in a footnote, that the sample depended on which states had digitized data. I could not open the published JCE full text (ScienceDirect 403, Nottingham repository behind Cloudflare). My web search budget ran out during this check, so I relied on direct DOI and repository lookups.

needs_fix.corrections: Bibliographic fields are correct (AER 96(3): 863-876, 2006; NBER WP 12003). Corrected finding: using state (Florida) and federal (California) data and several designs, including instrumental variables based on randomly assigned judges with different sentencing propensities, the paper finds 'no consistent evidence of adverse labor market consequences of longer incarceration length.' Judges' differing harshness is the instrument the paper relies on, not a result it 'established', so drop or soften the second sentence.

needs_fix.title: The Effects of Pretrial Detention on Conviction, Future Crime, and Employment: Evidence from Randomly Assigned Judges
needs_fix.corrections: Bibliographic fields are correct (Dobbie, Goldin, Yang; AER 108(2): 201-240, Feb 2018; doi 10.1257/aer.20161503). Corrected finding: using quasi-randomly assigned bail judges and court and tax records, pretrial detention significantly raises the probability of conviction, mainly through more guilty pleas. needs_fix.title: 憲法法庭113年憲判字第8號判決 (Constitutional Court Judgment 113-Hsien-Pan-8, death penalty)
needs_fix.corrections: Use the official source (https://cons.judicial.gov.tw/docdata.aspx?fid=38&id=351689) as the URL; the judgment was issued 20 Sept 2024 and is titled 死刑案. Corrected finding: The death penalty for Criminal Code 271(1), 226-1 (first clause), 332(1) and 348(1) is constitutional only where the case is among the most serious (intentional killing) and the procedure meets the strictest due-process standards. Main text item 7: no death sentence where Art. 19(2) applies at the time of the offence, i.e. the mental condition significantly diminished the defendant's capacity. Item 8: no death sentence where, at trial, a mental disability makes the defendant's capacity to defend themselves markedly insufficient, even if Art. 19(2) was not met at the time of the offence. Item 9: no execution where a mental condition, short of insanity, impairs competency for execution (受刑能力). Remove the claim that a requirement to prove the condition affected judgment was 'removed'. That is Wikipedia's gloss, not a holding, and the bar is not a blanket one for all defendants with mental conditions. Other holdings: mandatory defence counsel at interrogation and in the third instance, mandatory oral argument at the Supreme Court, and unanimity of the judicial panel for death sentences. Most items require amendments within 2 years (correct). Huang Lin-kai (黃麟凱) is petitioner no. 15 of 37. The NHRC statement of 16 Jan 2025 is confirmed as described.
needs_fix.note: I read the official main text (items 1-17 and reasons para 114-130). The Taipei Times (21 Sept 2024) wording 'even if the condition did not influence the offense' loosely describes item 8 (trial-time self-defence capacity). Items 7-9 each carry a 2-year amendment deadline and bar death sentences or executions in the meantime. The NHRC statement (posted 114-01-16) says executions should not proceed before the judgment's issues are clarified and regrets that day's execution. Huang appears in the judgment's petitioner list (no. 15), and Wikipedia says he was executed the day after 15 Jan 2025.
